question: A team plans to bring Claude into a workflow that three other departments feed into. Which step is most important before the change goes live?
options: A) Wait until the other departments adopt the same arrangement themselves
B) Tell the feeding departments what changes for them and what does not
C) Give each department its own version of the new written instructions
D) Ask the departments to stop sending work until the change is settled
correct_answers: B) Tell the feeding departments what changes for them and what does not
explanations: Making the change conditional on three other departments adopting it first blocks a workflow improvement that is entirely within this team's control.
Correct. Integration touches everyone who feeds the workflow. Being explicit about what changes for them, and what stays the same, is what stops the redesign breaking at its handovers.
Separate instruction versions per department guarantee that the workflow behaves differently depending on who fed it.
Halting incoming work to make an internal change imposes the cost on other departments unnecessarily.
